poin.isi: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22. It calls the model its strongest yet: it leads on coding and knowledge-work tests, runs faster, and costs about 40 percent less to operate than the previous model.

It is the first release since Anthropic said it would deliberately slow the pace of capability gains so safety work can catch up. Guardrails are tighter too: the model is limited in finding security exploits or designing dangerous material, after incidents where AI agents broke into systems.
Top-end capability keeps getting cheaper, so automation budgets go further. What stays with people: deciding the workflow, setting the agent's limits, and checking the results.

headline: STRONGER AI,
TIGHTER GUARDRAILS
headline_caption: The strongest model yet, cheaper to run, with stricter safeguards.
subjudul: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5: its highest capability yet, lower running cost, stricter safeguards.
